Three accepted extractions route it to ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.2/R02.4: PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-ETAL-25/84 (the same Artin–Tate X Thm. 5); PAPER-BOXER-CALEGARI-GEE-PILLONI-21/189, whose route reason says the Allen et al. and BCGE routes send 'square roots of characters and the Grunwald–Wang globalization of local characters here'; and PAPER-ALLEN-ETAL-23/328. The p. 69 quotation matches, and /210's locator omits that use. Corrections. 'BCGP-21/189(i) is exactly Lemma 7.10's p = 2 content' overstates: both are square-root-after-base-change statements with the same Grunwald–Wang input, but their local conditions differ. And the split is wider than claimed. The InverseGalois packet itself lists 'the global duality and Grunwald–Wang inputs' as remaining coverage, and PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-23/130 is accepted at IG.4, so re-routing /210 alone does not give the theorem one owner. R02.x and IG.4 are unrelated on the atlas, and every candidate owner is acyclic for KW II's consumers. Adjusted fix: in the extraction, move /210 (adding 'proof of Lemma 7.10, p. 69' to its locator) and /252 to R02.2/R02.4, beside the three accepted routes, and drop route 8. For the maintainer: the IG packet's coverage, HW-23/130 and the R04.4 hypothesis sentence must follow the same choice. If IG.4 is preferred, the three R02.x routes move instead. Either way, one owner states Grunwald–Wang in general form, with its special case.

Confirmed. Theorem 6.1 covers p = 2 (pp. 53–54). On p. 55 the paper asserts: 'For p = 2 one proves the existence of points with values in Q2 or Qpi, pi auxiliary prime, as for p ≠ 2'. No item records this. /193 covers only the real points. Every Taylor node and every R23.2 local-points node assumes an odd residual characteristic: 'Let l be an odd prime', 'Let l > 2', and Taylor's matching of level structures 'for l, p odd'. The R23.3 KW node has proof steps for the p = 2 real points and for k(ρ̄) = 4, but none for these local points. No source issue records the step either. Corrections. [34] is KW's paper on two-dimensional mod p representations, not a 2-adic paper; it is cited on p. 56 only for the ordinary k(ρ̄) = 2 branch. And 'missing' is not the only defensible status. The R23.2 stage text plans 'every prescribed finite local point', and the extraction marks the parallel p = 2 real-point step /193 as planned at R23.2 and H6, with a 'no node states it' note. Adjusted fix: add the item as proposed, with /193's status for consistency. The stricter alternative is missing on a source route to R23.2; either way R23.2 is the owner, and it is upstream of R23.3. The item's note says that the nodes assume l odd and that KW give no argument. The notes of /185, /186 and /204 say their p = 2 cases depend on it. The p. 55 sentence may also be recorded as a gap (affects: the proof). The request to R23.2 cannot be made by the fix job, which may edit only the extraction, so it becomes a note for the maintainer.

Confirmed. For p odd, §3.2.2(i) (p. 23) gives the weight-two lifts the inertial parameter (ω_p^{k(ρ̄)−2} ⊕ 1, 0). At k(ρ̄_p) = 2 this is the trivial type, so the lifts are crystalline of weight 2 and their ring is the smooth one of §3.2.3. k = 2 does occur for irreducible ρ̄_p, e.g. ρ̄|I_p ≅ ω₂ ⊕ ω₂^p. §3.2.4 (p. 24) applies Savitt's O[[T1, T2]]/(T1T2 − p) with no restriction on k. It makes the crystalline identification at p = 2 but not at k = 2 for odd p. R08.4/savitt-weight-two-rings states Savitt's ring for τ = ω̃^i ⊕ ω̃^j with i ≢ j mod p − 1. KW's type has i = k − 2 and j = 0, so the hypothesis holds exactly when 3 ≤ k ≤ p. The two rings differ: the special fibre 𝔽⟦T⟧ is regular, while 𝔽⟦T1, T2⟧/(T1T2) is not a domain. Both satisfy Theorem 3.1's properties, and the paper uses Savitt's explicit ring nowhere else, so 'affects nothing' holds. No existing source issue records this. The fix stands for /92, /93 and the new source issue. The request to restrict R08.6/export-weight-two-irreducible is not available to the fix job, which may edit only the extraction, so it becomes a note for the maintainer.

Confirmed. p. 24 says of §3.2.3's smoothness: 'There the case k(ρ̄p) = p and the case p = 2 is excluded, but as ρ̄p is irreducible the argument extends', and gives no argument. L7/fontaine-laffaille-deformation-condition has 'Fil^{l−1}M = 0' and Hodge–Tate weights in [0, l − 2], so it covers k ≤ p − 1 for odd p only. Correction: R08.6/export-fontaine-laffaille-irreducible does state k ≤ p and 'The same holds for p = 2 (k = 2)'. What it lacks is an input that proves those cases: its prerequisites are L7 and R08.1 only. So under §16 /91 is planned at a node that states it, and 'planned for k ≤ p − 1 only' overstates. The defect is in the node's proof and in /91's note. Adjusted fix: keep /91 planned, and rewrite its note. L7 covers k ≤ p − 1. k = p comes through FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.3/fl-full-faithfulness on MF′, since irreducibility keeps every deformation in MF′. p = 2 comes through R07.4 and R08.5, since R07.3 sends weight-one objects at p = 2 there. The paper only asserts the extension. The node's missing prerequisites are a note for the maintainer, since the fix job cannot file requests.

Confirmed. /273 describes Corollary 3.1.11 as: 'when the p-torsion of the cokernel of the degeneracy map … has only Eisenstein maximal ideals in its support, ρ̄ arises from a π_i with U′_i-invariants that is Steinberg at the new place'. That is the Ihara input: Kisin's (3.1.8), and KW's Lemma 7.1 (/222). I read the published corollary in Annals 170 (2009), p. 1151 (the Annals PDF, SHA-256 076f8bb6…4ee7). It reads: 'Let m ⊂ T^univ_{S_p,O} be a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal. Suppose that S_{σ,ψ}(U, O)_m ≠ {0} and that (T_λ² − (N(λ) + 1)²ψ(λ))(S_{σ,ψ}(U, O)) ⊂ m S_{σ,ψ}(U, O). Then the quotient S_{σ,ψ}(U′, O)_m / i(S_{σ,ψ}(U, O)²_m) is a non-zero free O-module.' Its proof begins: 'That the quotient is torsion-free follows from (3.1.8).' So /273 omits the congruence, the one hypothesis level raising needs, and without it the parenthetical is false. On p. 77 KW use Lemma 7.1 for the Eisenstein kernel and then apply Corollary 3.1.11. The congruence at v_{i+1} is left implicit there. It holds because ρ̄_F is unramified away from p (Lemma 8.1, p. 70) and the lifting data at v_j have the shape (γ_vχ_p ∗; 0 γ_v). Medium fits. High would also be defensible, since the item states something false, but the fix job is the same. The fix stands, with one adjustment: Lemma 3.5.3's tower (places above v_j inert except at step j) is already in /273's statement. So only the corollary's hypotheses, its conclusion and the source of the congruence need adding.

Confirmed for /314. R24.4/kw-theorem-4-1 states all of KW I Theorem 4.1, but its proof is 'Residual inputs (α), (β)', 'Allowable base change', 'Theorem 9.7 over F', 'Descent to ℚ'. Theorem 9.7 (p. 89) needs F unramified at p and lifts of types (A)–(C) (p. 75), and (A) allows k = p + 1 'only when F is split at p and k(ρ̄) = p + 1'. So it cannot give a potentially Barsotti–Tate lift whose type stays non-trivial over ℚ_p^nr(μ_p) after twisting (niveau-2 or wild types), nor the crystalline weight-(p + 1) case with k(ρ̄) = 2. §10.2 takes these from the literature (p. 92), as the Remark there says. R22.5/kw-odd-prime-lifting itself says that R24.4 assembles 4.1(2) from it 'and kisin-potentially-bt-lifting', which the R24.4 node omits. Corrections. /313 is included wrongly: KW prove 4.1(1) by Theorem 9.7 (p. 92), and R22.6/kw-dyadic-lifting states that range. And 'a type that needs a ramified extension never becomes (A)–(C)' is too broad: tame principal-series types trivialised over ℚ_p(μ_p) are type (B) up to twist. Adjusted fix: split only /314, reusing the extraction's own items: k ≤ p − 1 is /316; k = p and types (B)/(C) come from Theorem 9.7 through R24.4; k = p + 1 ordinary is /318; k = p + 1 non-ordinary, including k(ρ̄) = 2, is /317 (R21.5/blz-reduction-theorem with R32.2/odd-prime-de-rham-lifting, which stands in for Kisin [38], which no node states); potentially Barsotti–Tate is /319 (R22.5/kisin-potentially-bt-lifting (3)); potentially semistable but not potentially crystalline reduces to /318 by a finite-order twist. R22.5, R21.4 and R21.5 are upstream of R24.4, and R32.2 is unrelated to it, so nothing closes a cycle. For the maintainer: the R24.4 node should list these suppliers among its prerequisites, and the classical proof's use of R32.2 should wait for R32.6's globalisation audit.
